description: Language-agnostic qURL v2 conformance vectors: the single wire-truth every qURL v2 reader re-runs against its own implementation, including the share-safe qv2t1 outer transport and the unchanged canonical qv2 security grammar. Each class names the entry point it targets and the input shape it consumes; consumers feed the input through their real parser/validator and assert the declared accept/reject outcome and reject_class.
notes: All private keys in this artifact are public, fixed test material. Never admit the vector issuer key or kid to a production trust store, and never use the qURL-user or resource key outside conformance tests.

Every committed input is deterministic: keys are fixed bytes, derived from fixed bytes where a real keypair is required, or the exact keys carried by the composed signature fixture; none is freshly minted by a consumer.

claims_json / secret_json values are RAW JSON TEXT (ASCII), fed directly to parseClaims/parseSecret -- NOT base64. Duplicate keys and other JSON-layer faults survive because they live inside a JSON string value, not as object members a re-serializer would normalize away.
strict_base64 inputs are the base64url string VERBATIM (the fault is in the encoding layer); a consumer feeds them straight to its strict base64url decoder.

transport_fragment inputs are outer URL fragment bodies without the leading '#'. qv2t1 is the only accepted outer transport; legacy qv2 is accepted only after qv2t1 reconstructs it as the canonical inner security fragment.

A transport decoder rejects an input longer than max_transport_length before splitting or allocating by attacker-controlled counts. It then parses canonical bounded counts, validates chunk framing/alphabet, joins chunks in presented order, and emits the exact canonical_fragment bytes. It does not parse claims or authenticate signatures.

fragment inputs are canonical inner qv2 fragment bodies fed to ParseFragment, which does NOT verify the issuer signature -- the fragment class pins the unchanged security wire SHAPE only; signature accept/reject is the signature class. The fragment accept fixture carries a real X25519 proof-of-possession pair: its claims public key is derived from its secret private key.

The signature class is COMPOSED from issuer_signature_vectors.json (already byte-shared by the Go and TS verifiers); it is referenced here, not duplicated, so there is exactly one copy of the signature bytes.

KNK/ACK Noise handshake packet vectors live in the separate sibling artifact relay_knock_golden.json, not this one -- they belong to the Noise handshake layer, which the qURL v2 claims/signature/fragment layer does not import; the two families are split by layer.

signature_class.comment: Run the composed file's vectors through the issuer-signature verifier. accept => verifies; reject => fails with the declared reject_class (high_s | wrong_length). The composed file pins the P-256 raw r||s low-S wire encoding and the 0x00 domain separator across KMS sign output, Go verify, and WebCrypto verify.

tamper_derivation.comment: Language-agnostic payload-tamper reject DERIVED from the composed file's accept vector -- so every consumer (Go, other language implementations, the Go SDK) synthesizes the SAME negative without a third copy of signature bytes. Procedure: take the accept vector's valid 64-byte low-S signature UNCHANGED, and verify it against a claims input formed by flipping the FIRST character of the accept vector's claims_b64 between base64url 'A' and 'B' (i.e. 'A' -> 'B', any other char -> 'A'). The FIRST symbol encodes the top 6 bits of decoded byte 0 -- always fully significant, never a don't-care tail bit -- so the transformed claims_b64 stays CANONICAL base64url AND decodes to DIFFERENT bytes. That portability matters: a consumer may hash the base64 string (qURL v2's Go verifier does), decode-then-hash, or strict-decode before verifying; only a change that is both canonical and decoded-differing yields the SAME tamper rejection for all three. (A last-char flip would only touch a don't-care padding bit when len(claims_b64) mod 4 != 0, decoding to identical bytes and producing a non-canonical string -- not portable.) The signature stays structurally well-formed, so it passes the length/range/low-S gates and fails ONLY at the curve check: a verifier MUST reject it with its signature-invalid sentinel (Go: bare ErrSignature, NOT ErrSignatureHighS/ErrSignatureLength). This is the most basic signature negative -- a valid signature over the wrong message -- and is intentionally specified here as a derivation rather than stored bytes.

vectors.name: accept_valid_full
vectors.reason: schema-valid claims object with every required field, valid key lengths, and coherent iat<=exp / nbf<=exp bounds

vectors.name: accept_cell_id_absent
vectors.reason: cell_id is the one optional claim; absent entirely must still parse

vectors.name: reject_duplicate_key
vectors.reason: duplicate v key; a strict parser must reject (lenient last-wins is a signature-bypass hazard). The duplicate survives storage because it is inside a JSON string value.

vectors.name: reject_unknown_field
vectors.reason: extra is not in the claim allowlist

vectors.name: reject_null_required
vectors.reason: jti is null; a null in a scalar field must be rejected, not coerced to the zero value

vectors.name: reject_missing_required
vectors.reason: jti member dropped entirely

vectors.name: reject_float_time
vectors.reason: exp is fractional; integer time fields must reject a float

vectors.name: reject_string_time
vectors.reason: exp is a string; a string-where-int must be rejected

vectors.name: reject_array_for_scalar
vectors.reason: jti is an array; an array-where-scalar must be rejected

vectors.name: reject_wrong_version
vectors.reason: v is 1; the version is pinned to 2 and not negotiated from the payload

vectors.name: reject_nbf_after_exp
vectors.reason: nbf > exp; the clock-free ordering bound nbf<=exp rejects a structurally incoherent window

vectors.name: reject_short_cell_key
vectors.reason: cell_public_key_b64 decodes to 3 bytes, not the required 32; each key field is length-checked against its own size

vectors.name: reject_top_level_array
vectors.reason: top-level value is an array, not a single object

vectors.name: reject_trailing_data
vectors.reason: a second concatenated JSON value follows the object; a lenient parser would ignore it

vectors.name: accept_valid
vectors.reason: exactly one required field carrying a 32-byte X25519 private key in base64url

vectors.name: reject_unknown_field
vectors.reason: extra field x not in the secret allowlist

vectors.name: reject_missing_required
vectors.reason: empty object; the one required field is absent

vectors.name: reject_duplicate_key
vectors.reason: the private-key field appears twice; the DUPLICATE is the sole fault -- both values are the valid 32-byte key, so a length-check alone cannot reject this. A verifier that does not detect duplicate JSON keys (lenient last-wins) MUST still reject it, which is the signature-bypass hazard this isolates for cross-language consumers.

vectors.name: reject_short_private_key
vectors.reason: valid base64url but decodes to 3 bytes, not the 32-byte X25519 scalar; the PoP secret is length-checked at parse, not deferred

strict_base64.comment: Encoding-layer rejections a browser's lenient atob would silently accept. Two cases are load-bearing because they decode leniently to the SAME bytes as a canonical string, so the strict decoder must reject them to keep one string per byte slice (a signature-bypass guard and the cross-language agreement point on which STRINGS are well-formed): non-canonical trailing bits, and embedded CR/LF, which Go's base64 decoder skips in every mode (including Strict). A verifier that only strict-decodes, without a re-encode/round-trip canonicality check, will WRONGLY accept the embedded-whitespace vectors.

vectors.name: accept_canonical_32_byte_key
vectors.reason: canonical unpadded base64url of 32 zero bytes (43 chars)

vectors.name: reject_non_canonical_trailing_bits
vectors.reason: final char carries non-zero don't-care trailing bits; lenient decode yields the same 32 zero bytes but strict must reject

vectors.name: reject_padded
vectors.reason: trailing '=' padding is not in the unpadded base64url alphabet

vectors.name: reject_non_alphabet_char
vectors.reason: '+' is a standard-base64 char, not base64url; a '.' (the fragment separator) fails the same way

vectors.name: reject_length_1_mod_4
vectors.reason: a single base64url char cannot encode a byte (length 1 mod 4)

vectors.name: reject_embedded_lf
vectors.reason: an embedded LF inside an otherwise-canonical 43-char key; a browser's lenient atob silently skips '\n' and recovers the same 32 bytes, so the strict decoder must reject it to keep one string per byte slice

vectors.name: reject_embedded_cr
vectors.reason: an embedded CR inside an otherwise-canonical 43-char key; lenient atob silently skips '\r' and recovers the same 32 bytes, so strict must reject it

vectors.name: reject_embedded_crlf
vectors.reason: an embedded CRLF pair inside an otherwise-canonical 43-char key; lenient atob silently skips '\r\n' and recovers the same 32 bytes, so strict must reject it

fragment.comment: ParseFragment pins wire SHAPE and strict-parses the claims/secret parts; it does NOT verify the issuer signature, so the sig part need only be a base64url 64-byte blob. The accept fragment composes the signature fixture's accept claims part with a valid secret part and the fixture's accept sig. Reject fixtures intentionally retain their pre-rotation claims and signature bytes while using the canonical re-clamped secret because they isolate fragment shape failures, not issuer authentication.

vectors.name: accept_valid_fragment
vectors.reason: qv2 prefix, four dot-separated parts, strict-valid claims and secret, base64url 64-byte sig

vectors.name: reject_wrong_prefix
vectors.reason: prefix is qv1, not the literal qv2

vectors.name: reject_too_few_parts
vectors.reason: only three dot-separated tokens (prefix + claims + secret); the sig part is missing

vectors.name: reject_empty_sig_part
vectors.reason: four parts but the sig part is empty

transport.comment: Decode the share-safe outer URL fragment before ParseFragment. The decoder is framing-only: it rejects oversize input before splitting/allocating, accepts only qv2t1, parses three canonical bounded positive-decimal counts, requires exactly the declared chunks, enforces 1..240 base64url characters per chunk and exactly 240 on every non-final chunk in a field, enforces reconstructed field caps, and joins chunks in presented order. On accept it returns canonical_fragment byte-for-byte. Claims parsing and signature authentication remain downstream.

vectors.name: accept_valid_qv2_round_trip
vectors.reason: three claims chunks plus one secret and signature chunk reconstruct the existing canonical qv2 fixture byte-for-byte

vectors.name: accept_minimum_nonempty_fields
vectors.reason: one base64url character in each field is the minimum transport shape; the transport layer does not interpret inner qv2 semantics

vectors.name: accept_exact_component_boundaries
vectors.reason: 240-character claims and secret components plus the 128-character signature maximum are Apple-safe; a final chunk may be exactly 240 characters

vectors.name: accept_all_field_maxima
vectors.reason: 6144 claims characters, 512 secret characters, and 128 signature characters produce counts 26/3/1 and the exact 6826-character maximum transport

vectors.name: accept_equal_width_reordered_chunks_preserve_presented_order
vectors.reason: swapping two full-width claims chunks remains valid transport framing and must reconstruct in presented order; downstream qv2 parsing/signature verification, not transport, detects semantic tampering; the claims and signature retain their pre-rotation bytes while only the secret was re-clamped because this case tests transport framing only

vectors.name: accept_truncated_final_signature_preserves_presented_bytes
vectors.reason: removing bytes inside a still-nonempty final chunk is not detectable by framing; transport reconstructs exact presented bytes and the unchanged inner qv2 signature-length/verification gates reject downstream; the claims and signature retain their pre-rotation bytes while only the secret was re-clamped because this case tests transport framing only

vectors.name: reject_legacy_qv2_outer_transport
vectors.reason: legacy qv2 is the canonical inner security format, not an accepted outer URL transport

vectors.name: reject_unknown_transport_version
vectors.reason: qv2t2 is not a recognized transport version

vectors.name: reject_wrong_case_prefix
vectors.reason: the qv2t1 prefix is exact and case-sensitive

vectors.name: reject_zero_secret_count
vectors.reason: secretCount must be positive

vectors.name: reject_zero_signature_count
vectors.reason: sigCount must be positive

vectors.name: reject_whitespace_count
vectors.reason: counts do not accept surrounding whitespace

vectors.name: reject_nondecimal_count

vectors.name: reject_empty_count
vectors.reason: all three count tokens are required

vectors.name: reject_oversized_count_token
vectors.reason: an unbounded decimal token is rejected without integer overflow or allocation

vectors.name: reject_claims_count_above_maximum
vectors.reason: claimsCount is bounded at 26

vectors.name: reject_secret_count_above_maximum
vectors.reason: secretCount is bounded at 3

vectors.name: reject_signature_count_above_maximum
vectors.reason: sigCount is bounded at 1

vectors.name: reject_empty_claims_chunk
vectors.reason: every data chunk must be nonempty

vectors.name: reject_empty_secret_chunk
vectors.reason: every data chunk must be nonempty

vectors.name: reject_empty_signature_chunk
vectors.reason: every data chunk must be nonempty

vectors.name: reject_short_nonfinal_secret_chunk

vectors.reason: no data chunk may exceed component_max=240

vectors.reason: secret chunks contain base64url characters only

vectors.name: reject_signature_alphabet

vectors.name: reject_claims_field_above_maximum
vectors.reason: reconstructed claims length is bounded at 6144 even when all 26 chunks satisfy component framing

vectors.name: reject_secret_field_above_maximum
vectors.reason: reconstructed secret length is bounded at 512 even when all 3 chunks satisfy component framing

vectors.name: reject_signature_field_above_maximum
vectors.reason: reconstructed signature length is bounded at 128

vectors.name: reject_total_transport_above_maximum
vectors.reason: the 6826-character total bound is checked before splitting or count-driven allocation

vectors.name: reject_reordered_count_tokens
vectors.reason: claimsCount and secretCount are positional and cannot be swapped; the claims and signature retain their pre-rotation bytes while only the secret was re-clamped because this case tests transport framing only

relay_allowlist.comment: Pins the relay_url HTTPS + allowlist contract acted on only AFTER signature verification. Covers match PRECEDENCE (exact host:port vs bare-host-any-port), the userinfo embedded-credentials bypass, the http rejection, and fail-closed on an empty/absent allowlist. There is no entry-ORDER semantic in the matcher; these vectors pin precedence/coverage, not ordering of the entries slice.

vectors.name: accept_bare_host_default_port
vectors.reason: a bare-host entry matches a no-explicit-port URL: with no port, host == hostname, so the exact host[:port] lookup already hits (the bare-host-any-port fallback path is exercised separately by accept_bare_host_any_port)

vectors.name: accept_bare_host_any_port
vectors.reason: a bare-host entry matches any explicit port

vectors.name: accept_exact_host_port
vectors.reason: an explicit host:port entry matches the same host:port

vectors.name: reject_exact_host_port_other_port
vectors.reason: an explicit host:port entry does NOT match a different port for that host (precedence: the :8443 entry is literal)

vectors.name: reject_http_scheme
vectors.reason: scheme must be https

vectors.name: reject_off_allowlist
vectors.reason: host is on no allowlist entry

vectors.name: reject_userinfo_bypass
vectors.reason: classic allowlist bypass: the real host is evil.example.com with the allowlisted host smuggled into userinfo; userinfo-bearing URLs are rejected outright

vectors.name: reject_userinfo_real_host_allowlisted
vectors.reason: decisive case: even when the REAL post-@ host equals the allowlisted host, the userinfo guard (not the allowlist) must reject it

vectors.name: reject_empty_allowlist_fail_closed
vectors.reason: an empty allowlist rejects every URL (fail closed)

server_id.comment: The relay routing id the JS/headless agent derives from the cell public key for POST /relay/{serverId}: base64url(SHA-256(rawCellPubKey)[:8]), 11 chars, no padding. The consumer DECODES cell_public_key_b64 to raw bytes, recomputes the fingerprint with its OWN canonical implementation, and asserts it equals server_id -- so the routing contract is recomputed, never a trusted stored value. The fill-0x42 / fill-0x70 samples reuse the existing fingerprint golden inputs/outputs (crypto_fingerprint_test.go <-> fingerprint.test.ts) so this class cannot fork that contract.

vectors.name: cell_fill_0x44_fixture_cell
vectors.reason: the exact cell key carried by the composed signature fixture (32 bytes of 0x44)

vectors.name: cell_fill_0x42_golden
vectors.reason: reuses the fill-0x42 fingerprint golden vector input/output

vectors.name: cell_fill_0x70_substitution
vectors.reason: reuses the fill-0x70 golden vector whose 8-byte SHA-256 prefix exercises both base64url + -> - and / -> _ substitutions

vectors.name: cell_seq_1to32_golden
vectors.reason: reuses the seq-1to32 fingerprint golden vector input/output (cell key = 32 bytes of 0x01..0x20), shared with the relay-knock PubKeyFingerprint golden so the routing-id contract cannot fork
